---
title: "New Accounts and Idle Account Rate"
description: "Accounts created per day, and the share that never reached a partner service."
---

New CanadaLogin accounts per day, and how many of them never used a partner
service. A jump in the idle rate is a sign of bot sign-ups.

This is the one IBM Verify metric that reads the [raw event
stream](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_raw.qmd), because no summary table
records when an account first appears.

## Calculation

An account is **new** on the ET day of its first event in
[`authentication_activity`](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_raw/authentication_activity.qmd).
It is **idle** if it has no successful event in
[`application_usage`](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_raw/application_usage.qmd)
for a public relying party, one not flagged internal in
[`rp.service`](../../catalog/rp/service.qmd). The **14-day** variant also counts
an account as idle if its first public use came more than 14 days after its
first event.

Exclude the user ID `"UNKNOWN"`. Join to relying parties on alias, then
aggregate (see [Joining through the
lookup](../../catalog/rp.qmd#joining-through-the-lookup)).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
WITH first_seen AS (
    SELECT
        subject,
        min(CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)) AS first_ts
    FROM ibm_verify_events_raw.authentication_activity
    WHERE subject NOT IN ('', 'UNKNOWN')
    GROUP BY subject
),
new_accounts AS (
    SELECT
        subject,
        first_ts,
        -- time is a UTC string; report on ET days
        date(with_timezone(first_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto') AS created_on
    FROM first_seen
),
public_use AS (
    SELECT
        u.userid,
        min(CAST(substr(u.time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)) AS first_public_ts
    FROM ibm_verify_events_raw.application_usage u
    JOIN rp.alias al ON u.applicationname = al.alias
    JOIN rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
    WHERE u.result = 'success'
      AND NOT s.is_internal
    GROUP BY u.userid
)

SELECT
    n.created_on,
    count(*) AS new_accounts,
    count_if(p.userid IS NULL) AS idle_accounts,
    count_if(p.userid IS NULL OR p.first_public_ts > n.first_ts + INTERVAL '14' DAY) AS idle_accounts_14d,
    CAST(count_if(p.userid IS NULL) AS DOUBLE) / count(*) AS idle_rate,
    CAST(count_if(p.userid IS NULL OR p.first_public_ts > n.first_ts + INTERVAL '14' DAY) AS DOUBLE) / count(*) AS idle_rate_14d
FROM new_accounts n
LEFT JOIN public_use p ON n.subject = p.userid
-- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE n.created_on BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY n.created_on
ORDER BY n.created_on;
```

## R

```r
first_seen <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "authentication_activity")) |>
  filter(!is.na(subject), !subject %in% c("", "UNKNOWN")) |>
  mutate(ts = sql("CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)")) |>
  group_by(subject) |>
  summarise(first_ts = min(ts, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  # time is a UTC string; report on ET days
  mutate(created_on = sql("date(with_timezone(first_ts, 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto')"))

public_apps <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  filter(!is_internal) |>
  select(applicationname = alias)

public_use <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "application_usage")) |>
  filter(result == "success") |>
  inner_join(public_apps, by = "applicationname") |>
  mutate(ts = sql("CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp)")) |>
  group_by(userid) |>
  summarise(first_public_ts = min(ts, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

first_seen |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    created_on >= as.Date("2026-09-01"),
    created_on <= as.Date("2026-09-30")
  ) |>
  left_join(public_use, by = c("subject" = "userid")) |>
  mutate(
    idle = is.na(first_public_ts),
    idle_14d = is.na(first_public_ts) | first_public_ts > sql("first_ts + INTERVAL '14' DAY")
  ) |>
  group_by(created_on) |>
  summarise(
    new_accounts = n(),
    idle_accounts = sum(as.integer(idle), na.rm = TRUE),
    idle_accounts_14d = sum(as.integer(idle_14d), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    idle_rate = as.numeric(idle_accounts) / new_accounts,
    idle_rate_14d = as.numeric(idle_accounts_14d) / new_accounts
  ) |>
  arrange(created_on)
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

**Idle accounts are a signal, not a bot count.** Some real people sign up and
never use a service. Normal days run about 10% to 15% idle. On bot-wave days,
nearly all new accounts are idle.

**Compare months with the 14-day rate.** The "ever" rate keeps falling as
accounts have more time to reach a service, so recent days look worse than old
ones. The 14-day rate is final once 14 days have passed, so the last 14 days of
any window are still provisional.

**New accounts add up across days, rates do not.** Each account has one creation
day, so summing `new_accounts` or `idle_accounts` over days is correct. Recompute
a rate over a longer window from the summed counts.

**When an account appears.** Most new accounts first appear with a successful
password, which suggests the sign-up flow signs an account in once the password
is set, before any MFA. A few first appear through a token exchange instead,
possibly migrated accounts. Both readings are observed, not confirmed with the
sign-up flow's owners.

**It is expensive.** The query reads both raw tables from launch, and the cost
grows every month. Run it for a reporting window, not on a schedule.

## Alternative names

- new accounts
- sign-ups
- account creations
- registrations
- idle accounts
- dormant accounts
- accounts with no service use
